panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial chest CT of a real patient showing a small 4-mm ground-glass opacity in the lung (circled), the prototypical early CT manifestation of primary lung carcinoma (lepidic/adenocarcinoma spectrum). Article frames the lesion as mimicking primary lung carcinoma; final histology proved IgG4-related disease, so disease attribution rests on the carcinoma-typical imaging appearance and is therefore only moderately confident. B: Follow-up axial chest CT showing interval enlargement of the ground-glass opacity (circled) over 2.5 years, the classic growth pattern of an early lung adenocarcinoma. Same caveat as panel A: the lesion ultimately proved to be IgG4-related disease mimicking carcinoma. C: Axial chest CT demonstrating evolution of the lesion into a solid 9-mm nodule with spiculation and lobulation (circled), a textbook carcinoma-associated morphology (corona radiata/spiculated mass). Lesion was later shown to be IgG4-related disease...

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: B-scan ultrasound shows a diffuse homogenous retinochoroidal mass with subretinal fluid and medium internal reflectivity, consistent with choroidal metastasis from primary lung carcinoma per the article title and in-text mentions; no exact vocabulary finding applies. b: B-scan ultrasound shows a diffuse homogenous retinochoroidal mass with subretinal fluid and medium internal reflectivity, consistent with choroidal metastasis from primary lung carcinoma per the article title and in-text mentions; no exact vocabulary finding applies. c: Coronal CT chest shows an apical right upper lobe mass extending to the right hilum, directly demonstrating primary lung carcinoma; yellow circles are annotations.
panels.attribution_text: Bhatt et al. Regression of Bilateral Choroidal Metastases From Primary Lung Carcinoma in Response to Systemic Bevacizumab and Platinum Doublet.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.76900. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: At presentation. (a, b) B-scan ultrasound showing a diffuse homogenous mass lesion involving the retinochoroidal complex with subretinal fluid and medium internal reflectivity OU. (c) Coronal section of CT chest showing heterogeneously enhancing soft tissue density mass lesion (yellow circles) seen in the apical segment of right upper lobe extending up to the right hilar region. OS: oculus sinister; OD: oculus dexter; OU: oculus uterque.
in_text_mentions: arance. B-scan ultrasound (Nidek Co. Ltd, Aichi, Japan) showed a diffuse homogenous mass lesion involving the retinochoroidal complex with subretinal fluid and medium internal reflectivity OU (Figure 2a, Figure 2b). T-sign was absent, and no choroidal excavation or retinochoroidal calcification was noted. Based on the above clinical signs and multimodal imaging features, a provisional diagnosis of bilateral choroidal metastases was made.
